s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive central visual impairment with color vision defects and characteristic macular changes
salient_findings: Lifelong uncorrectable visual acuity and color vision impairment in the patient
Symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally on FAF imaging
key_facts: Patient is a 21-year-old woman
Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye
Myopia of –6.0 diopters
Intraocular pressures are 17 mmHg bilaterally
Fundus examination shows slight enlargement of the cup-to-disc ratio in both eyes
Visual field testing reveals a central scotoma in both eyes
FAF imaging demonstrates symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally
OCT shows thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea, partial preservation of the ellipsoid zone, and a normal retinal nerve fiber layer
ff-ERG reveals normal scotopic responses but attenuated photopic responses and 30-Hz flicker responses with delayed implicit times in both eyes
Family history of progressive blurred central vision and color vision defects in the patient's father
Father's best-corrected visual acuity is 20/200 in both eyes
Father's intraocular pressures are 17 mmHg in the right eye and 16 mmHg in the left eye

shortlist.label: Stargardt disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic macular changes with symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions and hyperautofluorescent borders, progressive central visual impairment, and family history

shortlist.label: Best vitelliform macular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Macular dystrophy with vitelliform lesions, central scotoma, and family history of progressive visual impairment

shortlist.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive central visual impairment, color vision defects, and attenuated photopic responses on ff-ERG

shortlist.label: Pattern dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Macular changes with hypoautofluorescent lesions and hyperautofluorescent borders, and family history of progressive visual impairment

shortlist.label: North Carolina macular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Macular dystrophy with central scotoma, and family history of progressive visual impairment

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of lifelong uncorrectable visual acuity and color vision impairment, central scotoma, and FAF imaging showing symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders are consistent with Stargardt disease. The family history of progressive blurred central vision and color vision defects in the patient's father also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Best vitelliform macular dystrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents with a characteristic 'egg-yolk' appearance on FAF imaging, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
rejected.why: Usually presents with more severe visual impairment and peripheral vision loss, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: Pattern dystrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents with a variety of patterns on FAF imaging, including a ' butterfly' or 'fishbone' pattern, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: North Carolina macular dystrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents with a slowly progressive course and often has a distinctive 'drusenoid' appearance on FAF imaging, which is not described in this case
